name: The Language Wars
description: Why there are so many programming languages, and how each one tried to fix the one before: from Ada Lovelace to Rust, Swift and Kotlin.

checkpoints.name: Before the code
checkpoints.note: Ada Lovelace imagines programs for Babbage's Analytical Engine, but for a century programmers must give machines numbers directly, and the idea of writing in words has to wait.

checkpoints.name: The pioneers
checkpoints.note: Fortran, Lisp, ALGOL and COBOL show that a computer can understand human-style instructions. BASIC opens programming to students, and each of these languages has descendants still in use.

checkpoints.name: Structure and C
checkpoints.note: Pascal, C, Smalltalk, SQL and Prolog set out new ways to organise programs and data. C becomes the language of Unix, and with it much of the world's software.

checkpoints.name: Objects everywhere
checkpoints.note: C++ and Objective-C bring object-oriented programming to ordinary work, Perl glues the early web together, and Python and Haskell start quietly.

checkpoints.name: The web era
checkpoints.note: Java, JavaScript, PHP and Ruby arrive in the same year or soon after, as the web creates demand for new languages. Microsoft answers with Visual Basic and C#.

checkpoints.name: Safer and simpler
checkpoints.note: Go, Rust, Swift, Kotlin and TypeScript aim at safety and speed, while Scratch teaches children. Each fixes a pain point of an older language, and none has replaced the old ones.
